summary: A sex offender registration arrest and a child endangerment arrest by sheriff's deputies Monday evening, and a judge kept the second man in the Spanish Fort bowling alley shooting jailed. Gulf Shores police warned of scams after a resident lost $4,000.

entries.title: Sex offender registration arrest: Robert Gordon McDuffie
body: Robert Gordon McDuffie, 62, was arrested by sheriff's deputies at 8:20 p.m. Monday, Oct. 26, and booked into the county jail on charges of failing to register as a sex offender, which covers an adult offender not registering with local police or not following residence restrictions, and first-offense drug paraphernalia.
He was in custody when the roster was read Tuesday morning.

entries.title: Child endangerment and marijuana arrest: Antonio Leverne Gibbs
body: Antonio Leverne Gibbs, 29, was arrested by sheriff's deputies at 7:21 p.m. Monday, Oct. 26, and booked on charges of endangering the welfare of a child, which covers putting a child's health or safety at risk, marijuana possession and first-offense drug paraphernalia.
He was in custody when the roster was read Tuesday morning.

entries.title: Bond revoked, Spanish Fort bowling alley shooting: Jamarcus Lawarren Grayson
body: Mobile County Circuit Judge Ben Brooks on Monday revoked the bond of Jamarcus Lawarren Grayson, 24, of Prichard, FOX10 reported. Grayson is one of the two men police say exchanged gunfire at Eastern Shore Lanes in Spanish Fort on Oct. 3.

Prosecutors say Grayson was under indictment in a 2024 shooting at a Mobile barbershop that wounded five people and was not allowed to have a gun. His lawyer conceded that point Monday and says Grayson acted in self-defense in both cases. He stays jailed until his trial in the 2024 case, set for April. The other man in the Spanish Fort case, Gregory McDonald, was booked Oct. 21 and released.

entries.title: DUI arrest by troopers: Darrell Joseph Williams
body: Darrell Joseph Williams, 39, was arrested by state troopers at 6:58 p.m. Monday, Oct. 26, and booked early Tuesday on a charge of driving under the influence of alcohol. He was the only admit in the jail's 24-hour list when it was read Tuesday morning, and was in custody.

entries.title: Scam warning, Gulf Shores: resident loses $4,000 to fake permit invoice
body: Gulf Shores police and the city warned residents and businesses on Monday about several active scams, FOX10 reported. The city says people who applied to its Planning Commission this year have received convincing emails and invoices demanding an "approval fee," and at least one resident lost $4,000.
The city says it never asks for payment by email wire transfer and asks anyone who receives such a request to contact the city directly. No arrest has been announced.
